focus: Caching: inventory every actions/cache, setup-node cache, bun and npm install and OpenCode install; find where caching is missing, keyed badly or defeated; size savings from step timings
answeredQuestions: Where is caching missing or ineffective for npm, bun, provisioned trees and OpenCode installs?

label: Fixed per-job overhead is 35.8% of sampled job wall: actions/checkout 26.6% (10,775s over 219 jobs, median 51s) versus install/provision steps 9.2% (3,742s). A warm install cache therefore has a ~340 min/day ceiling on the 3,812 billed min/day base, and checkout — not install — is the largest fixed cost, reachable only by fewer jobs or checkout shaping.

rg over .github/ finds no cache:, cache-dependency-path or actions/cache at all, and none of the 19 tracked package.json declares a packageManager field, so the automatic npm caching that actions/setup-node enables from that field never fires either; all setup-node calls pass node-version alone.

A node_modules cache is defeated by construction: the provision path runs npm ci which deletes node_modules, and actions/setup-node states it does not cache node_modules. The only legitimate payloads are the ~/.npm and ~/.bun/install/cache tarball caches (keyed across all lockfiles via cache-dependency-path) and the 5 dist build outputs the satisfied-walk checks.

The bun bootstrap npm install --no-save --prefix $RUNNER_TEMP/bun bun@1.3.9 runs at five sites across four workflows — opencode-dual-version.yml:101 and :184, opencode-plugin-tests.yml:69, hooks-node-tests.yml:60 and spec-kit-check.yml:100 — so iteration 003's claim that provisioning is confined to three workflows is too strong. Whether spec-kit-check calls provision_worktree after that line stays UNKNOWN.

OpenCode installs are 5-8s per leg and 11-14s for the both job, against a 60s provision in the same job; a dedicated OpenCode cache saves roughly 2 min/day and adds a second key space, so it is ruled out as a standalone optimisation and covered incidentally by the npm download cache.

Three key hazards make a naive cache unsafe: a package-lock-only key misses the bun-installed tree among 19 package.json; a prefix cache that omits matrix.family lets the v1 and v2 legs cross-restore and the battery can then pass on the wrong OpenCode version; and the both job installs both packages into the same key space. The safe shape is a lockfile+path-list key for tarball caches, a matrix.family-namespaced restore-only key for prefixes.

Install share of job wall is 51% (dual-version), 46% (plugin tests), 40% (routing-registry-drift) and 33% (hooks), but 7% in spec-kit-check and 2% in deep-loop-runtime — the two heaviest workflows by billed minutes — so caching is the dominant lever exactly in the four provision-heavy workflows and nearly irrelevant in the expensive long-suite ones.

The largest cache target outside the three provisioning workflows is routing-registry-drift's 'Install advisor scorer + build the shared projection dependency' at 88s median (81-114s range), which is install plus a tsc build, so its win is a compiled-projection artifact key rather than a download cache key.

Ten workflows request fetch-depth: 0 and their checkout medians (70-76s) sit above the depth-1 workflows (18-38s), but this is a 5-sample correlation on jobs that need base-ref diffs; a blob-filtered partial clone is the shape that keeps diffs and drops blobs, and it must be audited per consumer. Label: inferred.

direction: Caching OpenCode installs as a dedicated cache target
reason: 5-8s per leg and 11-14s for the both job, ~2 min/day across 7 runs/day, against the cost of a second key space; covered incidentally by the npm download cache.

npm ci deletes node_modules before installing and actions/setup-node documents that it does not cache node_modules, so the payload is either wiped or useless; only tarball caches and dist build outputs are legitimate.

direction: Enabling caching implicitly by adding a packageManager field to package.json files
reason: Zero of 19 tracked package.json declare it, and adding it to 19 files to obtain a cache is a wider and more semantically invasive diff than 35 explicit cache inputs.

direction: Ranking install caching as the top fixed-cost lever
reason: Install is 9.2% of sampled job wall against checkout's 26.6%; job-merge and checkout shaping move more minutes than any cache.
